title: AI in Production: What Breaks, What Works, and Who Approves It? | InfoQ Webinar
gist: InfoQ promotes a free Oct 14, 2026 panel on production AI covering agent autonomy, verification of AI-generated code, data exposure, production RAG and making the internal case for controls. It is promotional, with little hard data.

insights.claim: Once AI systems retrieve internal documents, generate production code, or act through tools, teams must be able to show what the system accessed, what actions were permitted, how output was verified and who is accountable on failure.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Governance and auditability are emerging requirements for enterprise AI adoption.
insights.locator: Once an AI system can retrieve internal documents

insights.claim: Platform and coding-agent teams want agents to do more, while privacy and security engineers want tighter limits, creating a tension the panel will examine.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agent permissioning and review gates are becoming a product and tooling category.
insights.locator: Building production AI puts two pressures in tension

insights.claim: Coding agents are moving from individual developers' machines into CI, and RAG pipelines are meeting sensitive or outdated data in production.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Production deployment exposes failures not seen in controlled tests.
insights.locator: Those questions become harder in production

insights.claim: The panel features practitioners from Thoughtworks and AI platform roles, including Lan Chu, whose QCon London 2026 talk argued production RAG is not easy and drew on systems with more than 10,000 documents.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Indicates practitioner focus on RAG reliability.
